whatTheyArgued: No text of hers on method was read. From the NEH 2016 humanities profile (read): she prepares by reading, watching or listening to the guest's work; her questions can be difficult but are 'not designed for attack or to result in cute sound bites'; she sets an atmosphere where guests volunteer answers; the NEH ties her skill to curiosity and understanding the guest's work. That is a description by others of a practice, not an argued thesis.

scholarship.ref: National Endowment for the Humanities, 'Terry Gross' (Humanities, Fall 2016)
scholarship.supports: preparation, curiosity, non-attacking difficult questions, guests volunteering answers
scholarship.disputes: none; it does not describe 'handing the thread back' or holding a claim to its ground

scholarship.ref: Wikipedia 'Terry Gross' via search summaries (SF Chronicle characterization: empathy, warmth, curiosity)

ourUse: earned-cast.js cues terry-gross on every question/assertion/escalation/frame-ask/map-ask and emits covert facts: reply plainly and hand the thread back; on pushback 'hold the claim to its ground, do not smooth the disagreement away'; on flatline 'draw the guest back out with a genuine question'. output-voice.js 'oral' register frame 'And here is what happened: X - label - Y.' labeled Terry Gross. output-claims.js calls its testimony register 'Terry Gross'.

bends.ours: The user is 'the guest' and the system 'draws them out'.
bends.theirs: Gross asks questions of a guest she researched; in chat the user asks and the system answers. The machine is in the guest's seat, so 'drawing out' maps only when the system asks a question back.

bends.ours: On escalation: 'this is where the conversation tightens - hold the claim to its ground, do not smooth the disagreement away.'
bends.theirs: Not found in any source read; NEH stresses questions that are not designed for attack. This is our epistemic rule under her name.

bends.ours: Compendium: 'let the answer be the guest's to reach, handing the thread back'.
bends.theirs: Closest supported statement is that guests volunteer rather than surrender answers; 'thread' language is ours.

bends.ours: Oral register opener 'And here is what happened:' and the testimony form (output-claims.js) are credited to her.
bends.theirs: Nothing in her practice implies either; these are our declared frames.
I could not read an interview or her own account of method; only a profile.
